text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on September 20 in history.

1519 - Ferdinand Magellan sailed from Seville, Spain, with a fleet of five ships in an attempt to circumnavigate the world. Only one, the Vittoria, completed the trip. Magellan was killed in a skirmish in the Philippines.
1697 - Treaty of Rijswijk (Ryswyck) was signed, under which England, Spain, Holland and the Holy Roman Emperor made peace with France at the end of the War of the Grand Alliance.
1746 - Bonnie Prince Charlie (Charles Edward Stuart) fled to France from Scotland following his unsuccessful attempt to capture the British throne.
1803 - Robert Emmet, Irish patriot, was hanged for his part in trying to seize Dublin Castle.
1833 - Ernesto Teodoro Moneta, Italian journalist, peace activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner in 1907, born.
1842 - Sir James Dewar, Scottish physicist and chemist who invented the vacuum flask, born.
1854 - The Battle of Alma was fought in the Crimean War. A combined British-French force defeated the Russians, opening the route to Sevastopol.
1863 - Jacob Grimm, German philogist and collector of folk tales with his brother Wilhelm, died.
1878 - Upton Sinclair, U.S. novelist and politician, author of 80 books, born.
1885 - Jelly Roll Morton (Ferdinand Joseph la Menthe Morton), U.S. jazz pianist, composer and singer, born.
1914 - Kenneth More, English film, stage and TV actor, born. Best known for his portrayal of the British World War Two fighter ace Douglas Bader in the film "Reach for the Sky".
1928 - The Grand Fascist Council became Italy's supreme legislative body, replacing the Chamber of Deputies.
1934 - Sophia Loren (Sofia Scicoloni), Italian film actress and Oscar winner in 1961 for her role in "Two Women", born.
1949 - The first government was announced for the Federal Republic of Germany.
1957 - Finnish composer Jean Sibelius died.
1962 - The prime minister of Southern Rhodesia, Sir Edgar Whitehead, issued an order banning the Zimbabwe African People's Union (ZAPU).
1967 - The British liner QEII was launched at Clydebank, Scotland.
1970 - The Soviet Luna 16 space probe landed on the moon and collected samples of lunar soil.
1973 - Billie Jean King defeated Bobby Riggs in a tennis match at Houston, Texas, billed as the "Battle of the Sexes".
1976 - The Swedish Social Democratic Party was defeated in parliamentary elections after more than 40 years in power.
1977 - Vietnam and Djibouti became the 149th and 150th members of the United Nations.
1978 - John Vorster announced his resignation as prime minister of South Africa for health reasons after 12 years in office.
1979 - Emperor Bokassa of the Central African Empire was deposed by former President David Dako who returned the country to the status of Republic.
1981 - Belize achieved independence from Britain.
1984 - U.S. embassy in Beirut was attacked by a suicide bomber who drove an explosive-packed truck into the compound, killing 40 people.
1989 - F.W. De Klerk was sworn in as president of South Africa.
1990 - The East German parliament and the West German lower house approved the treaty unifying the two countries.
1990 - Czechoslovakia rejoined the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank after a break of more than 35 years.
1993 - Azerbaijan's parliament voted to rejoin the Commonwealth of Independent States.
1994 - Member states of the International Atomic Energy Agency signed a new nuclear safety document designed to improve security at atomic reactors worldwide.
